tiers.none: Nothing is claimed. The agent may work, but ORCA says nothing about what its policy covers.
tiers.A: Connects and fails closed: the agent connects, first-run preflight recognises it, its docs exist, and every route ORCA does not cover is listed and refused or asked about, never silently allowed.
tiers.B: Approvals validated: tier A, plus every synthetic case runs on each of the agent's enforcement paths (or is excluded with a reason), and an unattended installed acceptance run against the pinned real agent proves ORCA's answers take effect there.
tiers.C: Execution guard certified: tier B, plus a connected proof receipt for this exact agent, version and host shows that what ran is what was approved, with no lifecycle or bypass case excluded unless it is listed as a residual risk.

paths.what: ORCA's answer to an ACP session/request_permission ask (resolvePermission, read fresh per ask by acp-session.ts)

excluded.F01: The ask arrives as an ACP request the SDK has already parsed; there are no raw bytes for ORCA to refuse.
excluded.F02: Decided in the session's own process; there is no separate context file to lose.
excluded.F03: Nothing is installed in the agent for this route.
excluded.P02: No raw input or context file on this route (see F01 and F02).
excluded.A04: An ACP ask carries no working directory; the session's directory is fixed when the session opens.

paths.what: ORCA's Claude Code PreToolUse hook (#704), run as its process runs it (runClaudePreToolHook)

excluded.L08: The hook's ask is handed to Claude, which sends it to ORCA as an ACP ask: covered on acp-ask.
excluded.F04: The hook never answers allow and offers no options; Claude's own options reach ORCA on acp-ask.

agents.tuple: Claude ACP adapter with Claude Code, Linux; no version pinned on main yet (#980 pins adapter 0.109.1 with Claude Code 2.1.330)

pendingRoutes.claude-native-hook: Turned on per agent by #980 (nativeToolHook: on); until it merges the hook is not reachable from a run

unsupportedRoutes: Tool calls Claude does not ask about (remembered grants, its own allow rules) until the hook is on
What a shell command touches beyond its own text
Remote sessions over SSH while the hook is on
residualRisks: A hook is not an operating-system boundary; Claude's sandbox and ORCA's protected-path rules stay in force beside it
agents.next: B once #980 merges: its claude-hook-acceptance.yml is the installed run. C after the #706 connected proof.
